title: The Miranda Hypothesis: How Hamilton Poisoned Persona Evals - Jacob E. Thomas, Results Gen

primary.label: Evaluation, Testing & Benchmarking
primary.rationale: The talk’s spine is measurement methodology: gold-standard in-character scores miss anachronistic compositing; he hands over a pre-registered 4×3×5 instrument, a 40/35/25 rubric that excludes voice, and a build-time expert gold-set gate. Implementation of companion is supporting evidence, not the subject.

secondary.label: Context Engineering & Memory
secondary.rationale: The proposed architecture is composing an encounter in the context window—prompt, primary documents, temporal anchor, human custody—versus dissolving the archive into fine-tuned weights.

secondary.label: Model Foundations & Behavior
secondary.rationale: The Miranda hypothesis is a claim about training-distribution overwrite and next-token compositing: models cannot distinguish a 1789 letter from a viral tweet, so output is a salience-weighted cultural composite.

secondary.label: Post-Training & Continual Learning
secondary.rationale: He argues RLHF amplifies the myth via algorithmic sycophancy, and that character fine-tuning plus catastrophic forgetting make specialization worse for this problem.

domains.label: Education & Learning
domains.rationale: Hello History, pedagogical personas, and historical simulation as civic/tutoring infrastructure are the shipped use cases he is measuring.

domains.label: Scientific Research
domains.rationale: The method is archival: historians in the loop, primary documents, pre-registration, and “bring language models into the archive.”

domains.label: Media & Creative
domains.rationale: Character AI companions and Hamilton/Spielberg cultural objects are the contamination source and a large deployed persona surface.

domains.label: Healthcare & Life Sciences
domains.rationale: The hospital-room dementia attempt is the ethical threshold, not a clinical product; Nature Medicine is an adjacent citation.

summary:
Thomas opens with Character AI, Hello History, and his open-source companion framework on Claude Opus 4.7, then asks an instantiated Lincoln when a president may take the country to war without Congress. The fluent answer sounds like Lincoln and is the wrong target. The in-character benchmark reports 80.7% personality alignment. Thesis: if the dominant failure is anachronistic compositing and evals measure fluency and personality consistency, they cannot detect it.

He is a data scientist who runs the analytics lab at a labor-market intermediary and ships production AI globally; he trained as a behavioral epidemiologist. Collaborators: Rick Halpern (University of Toronto) and Shawn Martin (Washington College). Chen 2024 and Wang 2026 survey RPLAs through rule-based templates, imitation, and cognitive simulation. Cooser (Wang) used ~18,000 literary characters; a 70B model matches or beats GPT-4 on three benchmarks. Character.eval uses 26 psychological indicators and graph memory. Those tools measure personality and register, not documentary constraint at a life moment. LLM-as-judge privileges fluency. Mask versus mirror: convincingness and fidelity are independent.

Hamilton is the paradigm. A frontier model reproduces the musical’s orphan-immigrant arc and a cleaned abolitionist, not Federalist syntax or the contested slavery record. Miranda hypothesis: culturally dominant representations exceed the primary record; next-token prediction cannot tell a 1789 letter from a 2019 tweet, so output is a salience-weighted composite that matches no verifiable moment. Federalist Papers ~175,000 words; musical-downstream content dominates. Schuyler Mansion visits nearly tripled after the premiere. RLHF amplifies the myth because raters share it—algorithmic sycophancy. Time-locked models (Varnum) change the contamination window but still average the figure.

Fourth stage: epistemic simulation—corpus-bounded, temporally anchored, expert-loop evaluated. For role-playing only, the unit is a five-part role-playing language system: structured prompt, primary-document anchors, temporal anchor, off-the-shelf model as voice not mind, human curator. The persona is a versionable configuration (context engineering), not a checkpoint. Context-window RAG keeps provenance; fine-tuning dissolves the archive and can amplify the composite. A 2026 Nature Medicine study found general-purpose models beat specialized clinical tools; biomedical fine-tunes show catastrophic forgetting. Context-window work is kitchen-table accessible; fine-tuning is institutional.

Prism instrument: four Lincolns (1847 Whig, 1858 Free Soil, 1860 unionist, 1862–65 emancipator) × bare / primary / biography seeds × five diagnostic questions = 60 units. Rubric: anachronism 40%, documentary consistency 35%, plausibility 25%; voice is excluded. Pre-registered, not run at scale. He shows the observed bare-model failure (20th-century “inherent executive authority”; Spielberg’s “clothed in immense power”) against the 15 Feb 1848 Lincoln–Herndon letter. Protocol: Miranda-condition figure, expert-locked moments, three conditions, blind scoring. Expert authors a gold-set gate at build/regate time, not runtime. The work began trying to restore language for a person with dementia; unanchored output was a cultural composite. If you ship persona systems, current evals measure the wrong thing; run the instrument in parallel.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.
temporalContext: Transcript claims reflect the publication date; linked external context was checked at the run's research date.
takeaways: Persona evals that score fluency and personality consistency cannot detect anachronistic compositing, the dominant failure of historical RPLAs.
The Miranda hypothesis: culturally dominant representations overwrite a figure’s documentary record in training corpora and in public memory.
Convincingness (the mask) and documentary fidelity (the mirror) are independent properties.
RLHF and human preference amplify the composite because raters share the same cultural myth—algorithmic sycophancy.
Epistemic simulation constrains a persona to a primary corpus, a temporal anchor, and expert-loop evaluation.
For role-playing, treat the unit as a five-part role-playing language system in the context window, not a persona in the weights.
Fine-tuning a character merges documentary signal with cultural sediment and breaks auditability; context-window anchoring keeps receipts.
A pre-registered Lincoln matrix (4 moments × 3 conditions × 5 questions) scores anachronism 40%, documentary consistency 35%, plausibility 25%.
A domain expert is a build-time and gate-time requirement, not a runtime cost; LLM-as-judge cannot see the archive.
The protocol is published as an instrument and invitation; no scaled results are claimed.

sections.title: Opening demos and the question of what evals measure
sections.summary: Character AI, Hello History, and the speaker’s open-source companion on Claude Opus 4.7 introduce RPLAs. A fluent Lincoln war-power answer sets up the formal question: what is the eval actually measuring?

sections.title: In-character 80.7% and the speaker’s measurement stance
sections.summary: The in-character benchmark’s 80.7% is a passing grade that can still miss a Broadway Hamilton. Thomas situates himself as a production-AI data scientist and former epidemiologist working with historians Halpern and Martin.

sections.title: Field trajectory: mask versus mirror
sections.summary: Chen/Wang surveys and Cooser/Character.eval show cumulative progress on personality fidelity. Those instruments cannot constrain a figure to a documentary moment; convincingness and fidelity are independent.

sections.title: Hamilton composite and the Miranda hypothesis
sections.summary: Model Hamilton inherits the musical’s register and a smoothed abolitionism. Three hypothesis claims cover corpus dominance, next-token compositing, and unauditable output. Alignment and time-locked models do not restore persona anchoring.

sections.title: Epistemic simulation and the role-playing language system
sections.summary: Fourth stage: corpus-bounded, temporally anchored, expert-evaluated. For RPLAs the unit is a five-part configured encounter; the persona is versionable context engineering, not a weight checkpoint.

sections.title: Context window versus fine-tuning, ethics, and access
sections.summary: Fine-tuning merges documentary signal with cultural sediment and breaks provenance. Nature Medicine and catastrophic-forgetting citations argue against specialization. Context-window architecture is archival, auditable, and kitchen-table accessible.

sections.title: Lincoln prism: pre-registered matrix and rubric
sections.summary: Four Lincolns × bare / primary / biography seeds × five diagnostic questions. Weights anachronism 40%, documentary 35%, plausibility 25%. Predictions and instrument are locked before data collection.

sections.title: Observed bare-model failure, protocol, and hospital-room stake
sections.summary: 1847 bare-model Lincoln uses 20th-century executive-power language versus the 1848 Herndon letter. Expert-authored gold sets are build-time gates. The work is accountable to unanchored composites of beloved persons, not entertainment bots.

organization.name: Results Generation
organization.summary: Results Generation (Results Generation Group, LLC) is an Austin recruitment-marketing company whose homepage describes a candidate-delivery platform that uses data, automation, personalized job alerts, and XML/API partner integrations across 13 markets. Jacob E. Thomas, the speaker, says he runs the analytics lab at a labor-market intermediary and ships production AI at global scale; the AI Engineer listing and his LinkedIn name that employer as Results Generation. COMPANION, the implementation in this talk, is Thomas’s open-source protocol (GitHub jethomasphd / the-companion-dossier.com), not the company’s job-alert product. Character.AI is a repeatedly named vendor example, not the owner.
organization.status: Independent Austin recruitment-marketing company as of the research date. Homepage, leadership page, and © 2026 Results Generation Group, LLC footer are live. Reported scale on the homepage: 300M job alerts/month, 150 recruitment partners, 13 global markets.
